items.title: Time-Aware Explainability for Cryptocurrency Forecasting: Evidence from a User Study
items.abstract: Abstract As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into financial decision-making, concerns about model opacity and regulatory compliance have come to the forefront. These concerns are particularly important in settings where forecasts influence risk assessment, portfolio decisions, and the credibility of AI-supported financial advice. This study examines how eXplainable AI (XAI) techniques can enhance transparency in the context of cryptocurrency forecasting–a domain characterized by extreme volatility and uncertainty. Using historical Bitcoin prices and macroeconomic indicators, we compare two deep learning approaches and apply TimeSHAP, a sequentially-aware explanation method, to clarify their predictions. Rather than focusing solely on model performance, we assess how different explanation formats are interpreted by finance-oriented users through a structured user study. Results show that local explanations are more easily understood and perceived as actionable, while more abstract forms–such as event-level and global plots–elicit mixed responses. This distinction matters because the practical value of explainability in finance depends not only on technical faithfulness, but also on whether explanations improve users’ confidence, support better-informed decisions, and help institutions justify model-based actions under scrutiny. To further support transparency and regulatory alignment, we document the entire machine learning process using a domain-specific ontology (XMLPO), offering a structured approach to traceability and reproducibility. Our findings suggest that effective explainability in financial AI requires both technically robust methods and communication strategies tailored to the needs of end-users. For financial economists and policy- and decision makers, the results indicate that the format in which AI explanations are presented can shape trust, perceived usefulness, and the governance value of predictive systems. This study contributes to the growing body of work on how AI systems can be made more interpretable, trustworthy, and aligned with economic governance in high-stakes domains.

items.title: To Learn is to Wander: Learning Across Graphs and Tasks with Random Walks
items.abstract: Graph foundation models aim to transfer across graphs, feature spaces, relational schemas, and prediction tasks, yet existing approaches typically generalize only within particular graph modalities or tasks. We propose Wander, a graph foundation model designed to operate across these settings within a single pretrained checkpoint. Following the prior-predictive perspective, we formulate graph learning as completion of a partially observed graph. We realize this task-general view through a common interface based on random walks, allowing the same model to operate across homogeneous and multi-relational graphs with varying features, labels, and relational schemas. Wander can increase its structural context at inference time without changing its learned parameters and, under suitable assumptions, universally approximates the corresponding Bayes-optimal predictor on bounded connected graphs. Empirically, a single pretrained checkpoint achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive results across node classification, homogeneous link prediction, and knowledge-graph link prediction. Moreover, joint pretraining across graph modalities and tasks preserves performance in specialized settings while enabling positive transfer and the composition of separately learned capabilities at inference time.

items.abstract: Top 5 Upcoming Data Center Projects in Tennessee 2026 Tennessee is emerging as a growing destination for data center development, with AI and high-performance computing driving new investment across the state. Blackridge Research tracks 10 upcoming data center projects in Tennessee, representing approximately 380 MW of planned capacity and USD 4.6 billion in construction expenditure. The pipeline includes projects at planning, announced, under-construction, and contract-award stages. Major developments include xAI's Colossus campus in Memphis, Meta's Gallatin campus, and new AI-focused projects in McMinnville, Knoxville, and other Tennessee markets. These developments span AI infrastructure, hyperscale facilities, and emerging digital infrastructure projects. This article examines the top 5 upcoming data center projects in Tennessee, comparing their capacity, location, developer, investment, development stage, and expected timelines. List of Top 5 Upcoming Data Center Projects in Tennessee, USA xAI Colossus AI Data Center Campus (Tulane Road expansion) xAI is expanding its Colossus AI data center campus in Memphis, Tennessee, into one of the largest single-site AI computing developments in the world. The expansion includes a third building near the existing Colossus facilities and is planned to bring the overall campus to approximately 2 GW of power capacity and more than 555,000 NVIDIA GPUs. xAI has invested heavily in the Memphis campus to support large-scale training of its Grok AI models. Meta Gallatin Data Center Meta’s Gallatin Data Center is a large-scale greenfield data center campus in Gallatin, Tennessee, spanning approximately 900 acres. The multi-building campus is planned to include up to 12 data halls and two administrative buildings, with more than 1.5 million square feet of total infrastructure. The project represents an investment of more than USD 1.5 billion in Tennessee and is designed to support Meta’s expanding cloud, social media, and AI infrastructure. Cielo Clarksville Data Center Cielo Digital Infrastructure is planning the Cielo Clarksville Data Center on approximately 107 acres in Clarksville, Montgomery County, Tennessee. The purpose-built campus is planned as a scalable, multi-building data center development designed to support high-density computing while limiting water consumption. The project represents an estimated USD 6.6 billion investment in the Clarksville community, including the infrastructure and mechanical and electrical systems required for long-term operations. Located at 5101 S National Drive, the campus has approximately 86 MW of total power capacity and is being developed through a phased AI conversion program. Bitdeer is targeting completion of the initial conversion phase in late 2026, with further development planned for 2027. Hixson Data Center The Hixson Data Center is a planned 25 MW AI data center campus in McMinnville, Warren County, Tennessee. Developed as a purpose-built facility for high-density GPU workloads, the project will span approximately 96,065 square feet across two levels and is designed to support NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 systems. The campus is planned as a single-tenant facility, with completion targeted for Q1 2028. items.title: Toward an operational predictive maintenance 5.0 framework informed by a scoping review and an industrial case study
items.abstract: The transition toward Industry 5.0 (I5.0) is reshaping industrial systems around sustainability, Human-Centricity (HC), and resilience, yet most Predictive Maintenance (PdM) approaches remain focused on technical objectives inherited from Industry 4.0. To characterize the maturity of I5.0-aligned PdM research, a scoping review of the Scopus database was conducted, screening 238 articles and retaining 123 based on substantive-engagement criteria, followed by a weighted scoring protocol assessing the depth of engagement with the three I5.0 pillars. The review reveals a pronounced skew toward shallow integration, with only a minority of studies operationalizing sustainability, HC, and resilience jointly. Building on these findings, this paper proposes an implementation-oriented Predictive Maintenance 5.0 (PdM 5.0) framework structured around three interconnected layers. The framework introduces a structured Large Language Model-mediated human-in-the-loop interaction, an adaptive learning mechanism, and an energy and CO 2 estimation pathway linking equipment degradation to sustainability indicators. A preliminary industrial case study using operational data from a recycled-paper mill demonstrates the practical execution of three interconnected pathways of the framework: equipment health assessment, energy and CO 2 impact estimation, and human-in-the-loop interaction supported by LLM-mediated explanations. Layer-specific evaluation metrics are further proposed to support broader operationalization. This work contributes a scoping-review-grounded architecture that advances PdM from a purely technical function toward a holistic, I5.0-aligned paradigm, while providing initial empirical evidence of its operational feasibility and a structured basis for broader industrial validation.

items.title: Toward DOI-Based Mission Impact Tracking: An LLM Agent for SPASE Authorship Metadata
items.abstract: Measuring the impact of a scientific mission depends on knowing when its data are used, by whom, and how often. For decades, DOIs have been used to track citations of authors' publications; a similar mechanism can make an observatory or instrument a citable resource that serves as a connection to the various outputs it produces. SPASE's observatory and instrument records could support this, but minting a DOI requires an author list, which is notably lacking in the records and difficult to determine manually. This bottleneck, among others, stands between the community and DOI-based tracking of mission impact. We present an LLM-based agent that automates the discovery of candidate authors for existing SPASE instrument and observatory records. Its core is a curation procedure derived from manual practice and refined through community feedback. It searches sources in a prioritized order to extract information: the SPASE record's own contacts, Calibration and Measurement Algorithms Documents (CMADs), sibling instrument and observatory records, data-provider sites, and the published literature. Keywords, publication timing, author count, and citation heuristics identify the mission and instrument description papers, and author order is then used to extract potential authors. It then applies an evidence-strength hierarchy that distinguishes authors from incidental mentions, producing a candidate author list with per-source provenance links and confidence levels for human review. We describe the agent's architecture, its performance against manually validated test cases, and the central challenge of trust in AI-generated metadata. We close by outlining future directions, including extending this approach to other metadata fields in SPASE observatory, instrument, and dataset records to support impact measurement, citation, and discovery.

items.title: Toward Intelligent Quality Assessment of Camellia oleifera : A Safety-Nutrition-Flavor Framework and the Role of AI
items.abstract: Camellia oleifera, honored as the “oriental olive oil”, is a high-quality woody oil crop. This review constructs a multi-dimensional quality matrix as an integrated framework that cohesively links safety, nutrition, and flavor. Genetic, growth environmental and processing-related determinants of Camellia oleifera quality were thoroughly analyzed. The current applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in disease diagnosis, intelligent and non-destructive detection, maturity evaluation, and adulteration identification of Camellia oleifera are summarized. Regarding future prospects, research efforts may be directed toward the development of integrated systems for Camellia oleifera quality evaluation that are multimodal, interpretable, portable, and transferable across diverse cultivars.

items.title: Toward personalized shared decision-making: a pilot study on an individualized patient decision aid
items.abstract: Decision aids are tools that can reduce decisional conflict and enhance patient satisfaction in the decision-making process. However, tool heterogeneity and clinical barriers, such as physician time constraints, hinder their implementation. This study introduces an individualized patient decision aid, developed within the European I3LUNG project, to support shared decision-making (SDM) in non-small cell lung cancer. The present decision aid is a dynamic, online tool structured into five sections (overview, prognosis/treatments, comprehension quizzes, patient preferences, and support/FAQs) designed to improve communication and emotional regulation between physicians and patients. The tool was evaluated using focus groups with patients and oncologists, interviews, thinking-out-loud sessions, and an ad hoc 32-item questionnaire. Focus groups and semi-structured interviews highlighted patient anxiety and oncologist interest in streamlining consultations and managing distress. Thinking-out-loud sessions confirmed that the decision aid may serve as an effective clinical guide. In the questionnaire, patients reported high overall satisfaction, demonstrating its clarity and clinical feasibility. The present decision aid may represent an innovative digital tool to promote SDM by aligning healthcare decisions with patient preferences, engaging caregivers at home, and reducing clinician cognitive workload and burnout. Future longitudinal, cross-cultural research integrating artificial intelligence and advanced human factors will be essential to provide more equitable and effective decision support. While preparing this manuscript, we partnered actively with non-small lung cancer patients and oncologists, with whom we had regular interactions to get their valuable and insightful input in shaping our reflections.

items.title: Towards responsible AI in workplace-based assessment: a scoping review using Downing’s framework
items.abstract: This scoping review maps generative AI applications in workplace-based assessment (WBA) and analyzes validity evidence through Downing’s framework. Following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, four databases were searched (2022-February 2026) with dual-AI screening and human adjudication. Data were mapped to Downing’s five validity sources using AI-assisted extraction with human verification. Thirteen studies (2024–2025) met inclusion criteria. All AI applications operated on pre-existing text; feedback analysis predominated (9/13). Content (12/13), Response Process (13/13), and Relationship to Other Variables (12/13) were well addressed, while Internal Structure (2/13) and Consequences (4/13) were neglected. AI reasoning transparency, inter-model agreement, and internal consistency were absent (0/13). Current evidence concentrates on AI-human agreement, neglecting reproducibility, bias testing, and learner impact evidence essential for responsible deployment. Realising AI’s potential to reduce faculty burden will require non-supervisor oversight mechanisms for continuous validity monitoring, particularly for direct learner-facing applications.

items.title: Training-Free Transformer Merging via Sequential Local Operator Alignment
items.abstract: Training-free model merging aims to combine multiple fine-tuned models into a single model without further optimization on labeled data. Yet, in transformers, independently merging individual layers can affect a shared attention computation because the query-key and value-output operators depend on composed matrices, overlooking the functional structure. Moreover, when merging earlier components, downstream components receive different activations than they do in the original model, thus, the merged and original execution paths no longer match. In this paper, we introduce Sequential Local Operator Alignment, a training-free method that merges transformers along the execution path of the partially merged model. Our method uses calibration data to estimate the local behavior of each functional component, aligns operators sequentially under the intermediate activation of the partially merged model, and subsequently factorizes the merged operators back into valid transformer parameters. We empirically show that this sequential step reduces error accumulation across layers. Furthermore, the proposed operator factorization step enables rank expansion, providing a principled mechanism for increasing multi-task capacity. We demonstrate that our approach generalizes across modalities, model scales, and varying numbers of tasks, from CLIP and RoBERTa to billion-parameter LLMs, and further extends naturally to the merging of LoRA-fine-tuned models. The results indicate improvements over strong merging baselines without requiring rank expansion, while optional expansion provides a further accuracy-inference-cost trade-off. items.title: TranScope: What the Software Hides About LLM Training Data, the Hardware Reveals at Scale, and Accelerators Magnify
items.abstract: Membership is the root privacy primitive in machine learning: to date, no hardware-based out-of-distribution detection on black-box models has been demonstrated against constant-time, static neural networks with masked confidence. This paper performs the first cycle-level examination of how large language models and vision transformers interact with various modern microarchitecture components, including integrated accelerators, as LLMs scale in size and answers the question of whether the data that a model was trained on affects its execution footprint even without any input-dependent branch, dynamic optimization, or early exit and in constant-time models. The results confirm that the answer is yes and identify which modern hardware components, such as TLBs or on-core accelerators, reveal or amplify that effect. The results also answer whether the signal is informative enough to reliably classify the in-/vs/out-of-distribution property of membership. To understand why, we perform a systematic root cause analysis and find that the transformer's tokenization steps, which happen during training, alter the locality of the accesses the model makes to fetch the vocabulary token later during inference and, as a result, change the page table access patterns and TLB in a previously unknown data-dependent way, causing microarchitectural state to vary significantly based on whether or not the input was in the distribution of the transformer training data. Building on the above observation, we introduce TranScope: the first microarchitecture tool for detecting membership information with low cost, no need for a surrogate model, and significantly higher robustness, e.g., 0.6 AUC for PETAL (best previously reported) vs 0.9 AUC (ours). This reintroduces hardware as both an opportunity, e.g., a tool for checking copyright violation for the first time, and a new channel for inferring membership (MIA).

items.title: Transformative promise and implementation challenges: Health care managers' perceptions and experiences of artificial intelligence—A mixed-methods systematic review
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a technological development that offers new opportunities for managing health care services. PURPOSE: To identify and synthesize the best evidence on health care managers' and other professionals´ experiences and perceptions of the utilization of AI in management. METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: A mixed-methods systematic review was conducted following the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology using a convergent integrated approach, including qualitative and quantitative data synthesis followed by thematic analysis. A systematic search was conducted in January 2025 in Ovid Medline, CINAHL, Scopus, ProQuest and Medic, limiting studies between 2016 and 2025 and written in English, Swedish, or Finnish. FINDINGS: The results were reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA). A total of 16 studies from 10 countries were included, comprising 11 qualitative and 5 quantitative studies. Of the participants, 90% were health care managers, and 10% were other health care professionals, such as nurses, physicians, and developers. The thematic analysis identified five themes reflecting participants' perceptions and experiences: AI as a transformative mechanism, organizational enablers and outcomes of AI utilization, AI-supported operational and risk management efficiency, strategic financial benefits and long-term value creation through AI, and data-driven opportunities and challenges in AI utilization for health care management. PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Health care managers should strengthen AI-related competencies, data governance, and organizational readiness to support effective AI implementation. Leadership practices that foster innovation, workforce engagement, and responsible data-driven decision-making may help organizations realize the operational and strategic benefits of AI.

items.title: Transformer based FinBERT framework with explainable artificial intelligence for money laundering detection
items.abstract: The increasing complexity of suspicious financial activities has reduced the effectiveness of conventional rule-based monitoring for modern anti-money laundering (AML) applications. This study proposes FinBERT-AML, a transformer-based framework fine-tuned on transaction feature tokens to learn complex dependencies across heterogeneous financial attributes. Through self-attention-based representation learning, the framework jointly models categorical and continuous transaction characteristics while overcoming limitations associated with conventional machine learning and sequential architectures. Experimental evaluation on the SAML-D dataset demonstrates that the proposed leakage-free configuration, with the target-dependent Laundering_type attribute excluded, achieves an accuracy of 92%, outperforming conventional machine learning, deep learning, and tabular transformer baselines. Information-gain analysis is employed to assess feature relevance, while LIME and SHAP provide complementary local and feature-attribution explanations of individual AML predictions. Statistical significance testing further evaluates the reliability of the observed performance improvements.

items.title: TrustmeWatcher: An Application for Workplace Micro-Sensing and Explainable Well-Being Feedback
items.abstract: Workplace sensing studies combine long-running behaviour traces with self-reports, yet the tools that collect those data often sit apart from the interface that returns results. We present TrustmeWatcher, the application built for the TRUST-ME project to connect this work. TrustmeWatcher reuses ActivityWatch's OS-level watchers for computer-activity collection and adds its own application layer. It turns the collected traces into an interactive screen-time dashboard, synchronizes responses from short questionnaires completed on the StreamDeck, and presents questionnaires alongside video highlights. Activity records and self-reports are aligned into labelled records for model development. The scope of this paper is limited to ActivityWatch data as model input. Artificial intelligence (AI) uses these activity records to predict six normalized state scores and an overall well-being score. The trained model runs locally, and the dashboard presents its predictions in semantic bands. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) helps users understand how recorded activity contributed to a prediction. Privacy Control lets users pause or resume the camera and eye tracker used by the study. We describe the workflow, its user-device and sensing-setup boundaries, and its use with records from 17 participants. The result is a deployed application and study workflow that integrates activity review, study data collection, privacy control, local prediction, and a participant-facing interface for XAI evaluation.

items.title: Understanding Practices, Device Ecologies, and Challenges in Video-Based Software Learning: An Empirical Study and Design Opportunities
items.abstract: Video-based tutorials are a primary resource for learning feature-rich software, yet less is known about how learners coordinate tutorial viewing and software execution across device arrangements during authentic learning tasks. We conducted a mixed-methods study combining a survey of 87 learners with contextual inquiries involving eight participants. The survey characterized learning practices, device configurations, and frictions; the contextual inquiry analyzed pauses, rewinds, and task-blocking stuck moments as observable interaction breakdowns revealing underlying usability barriers. Findings show that frictions stem from insufficient input information, dense instructional pacing, preset or state mismatches, and missed or extra operations disrupting watch-and-do workflows. We identify design opportunities including input-action overlays, step-level segmentation, preset and state checkpoints, structured subgoal outlines, and coordination support across device ecologies. This work provides empirically grounded insights into situated video-based software learning and translates observed interaction breakdowns into actionable design implications.

items.title: Understanding social and scientific conflicts shaping modern wildlife conservation
items.abstract: India’s Project Cheetah (2022–2025) is a significant, high-stakes translocation effort aimed at re-establishing the cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) seven decades after its local extinction. This study employs concepts of sociotechnical imaginary and epistemic injustice to analyze the project's contested outcomes, with a focus on the interaction between scientific risk and governance failure. Project Cheetah reached a key milestone with the birth of 22 cubs; however, it was also marked by high initial mortality. By April 2025, the project recorded the loss of 8 adult founder cheetahs (40.0% of the original 20) and 5 cubs (22.7%). Although conservation efforts inherently involve biological risks, our analysis shows that the observed mortality rate exceeded expected ecological thresholds, with a significant concentration around institutional instability. An analysis of cheetah mortality patterns revealed a negative association between survival time and the period immediately following a critical change in project coordination, suggesting that governance disruptions may have contributed to increased mortality. This was worsened by a strong national sociotechnical imaginary of ecological revival, which often overshadowed transparent risk communication and scientific criticism. Limited stakeholder consultation and asymmetric information created conditions for testimonial and hermeneutical injustices, marginalizing the expertise of critical voices. The study concludes that the long-term success of large-scale, transnational rewilding projects depends heavily on institutional capacity, not just ecological suitability. Lessons learned highlight the importance of transparent data management, thorough and inclusive consultation, and honest communication of scientific uncertainty to stakeholders, building the trust needed to sustain such complex political and environmental initiatives.

items.title: VepAgent: Bridging Causal-Transition via Tool-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Video Event Prediction
items.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable potential in video understanding, yet their reliance on retrospective summarization and text-centric priors often limits their ability to bridge unobserved causal transitions when applied to Video Event Prediction (VEP). To address this, we propose VepAgent, an agentic framework that integrates causal-transition reasoning with tool-augmented reinforcement learning (RL) for robust VEP. Unlike prior methods that passively project future trajectories from historical dependencies, our approach explicitly models the logical progression from terminal observed states to future events. Specifically, we first construct futurebench-4K, a high-quality chain-of-thought dataset for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) that effectively bridges the causal-logic gap by structuring the deduction of unobserved intermediate states. Subsequently, we develop a diagnostic tool library integrating state tracking, frame retrieval, and region magnification, enabling the agent to dynamically augment reasoning with external tools to recover missing spatio-temporal evidence and resolve visual ambiguities during inference. Moreover, we propose a composite reward mechanism that jointly optimizes prediction accuracy, causal coherence, and reliable prior, compelling the agent to rely on genuine visual grounding rather than superficial textual similarities. Extensive evaluations on FutureBench and NEPBench datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming larger MLLMs and validating the empirical effectiveness of our agentic, future-oriented reasoning paradigm.

items.title: Verifying accident causation models: A comparative analysis of representational capabilities
items.abstract: Learning from accidents is a cornerstone of safety improvement in complex sociotechnical systems. Accident causation models play a central role in this process, yet evaluating such models remains challenging. Validation is particularly difficult for retrospective accident analyses, as no external ground truth exists against which model outputs can be directly compared. This study therefore focuses on verification: assessing whether accident causation models represent failures in accordance with their intended purpose. We define a set of verification criteria to assess how well models represent key features of complex sociotechnical failures, including those characteristic of construction systems. Using these criteria, we assess four accident causation models through three failure cases drawn from construction and spaceflight contexts. We compare the resulting graphical representations against systems thinking tenets and construction-specific failure features. The models differ in how they depict system interactions and causal structures, leading to distinct representational strengths and limitations. In particular, models vary substantially in their ability to capture temporal dynamics and the evolving structure of project-based organizations. The proposed framework supports the assessment and selection of accident causation models based on their representational capabilities. As systems grow more complex and operate in increasingly challenging environments, improving our ability to verify and select models remains essential for learning from accidents and designing for safety.

items.title: Vulnerable Coronary Plaques on CT Angiography: Imaging Biomarkers, Artificial Intelligence, and Emerging Technologies for Risk Stratification
items.abstract: Background: Coronary artery disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Increasing evidence has demonstrated that many acute coronary events originate not from severely obstructive lesions but from structurally unstable atherosclerotic plaques. Consequently, the identification of vulnerable plaques has become a major objective in contemporary cardiovascular imaging. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) has evolved from a modality primarily focused on luminal stenosis assessment into a comprehensive non-invasive technique capable of evaluating plaque morphology, composition, and overall coronary atherosclerotic burden. Results: Our review summarizes current evidence regarding the role of CCTA in the detection and characterization of vulnerable coronary plaques. Particular emphasis is placed on imaging biomarkers associated with plaque instability, including low-attenuation plaque, positive remodeling, spotty calcifications, and the napkin-ring sign, which have been consistently linked to an increased risk of adverse cardiovascular events. Advances in quantitative plaque analysis have further enhanced the ability of CCTA to assess plaque burden and monitor disease progression. Emerging technologies are rapidly expanding the capabilities of coronary CT imaging. Spectral CT techniques and photon-counting detector CT offer improved tissue characterization and enhanced visualization of plaque components. In parallel, artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms are enabling automated plaque detection, segmentation, and risk prediction, facilitating more precise and reproducible analysis of large imaging datasets. Conclusions: Despite these advances, limitations remain, including restricted spatial resolution for microstructural plaque assessment and the limited ability of conventional CT to directly evaluate biological processes such as inflammation. Future developments integrating advanced CT technologies, artificial intelligence, and multimodality imaging are expected to further improve the non-invasive identification of vulnerable plaques and personalized cardiovascular risk stratification.

items.title: Watermarking: from Impossibility to Auditable Compliance
items.abstract: Article 50 (2) of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act requires providers of generative systems to make synthetic outputs machine-readable and detectable, while qualifying the effectiveness, interoperability, robustness, and reliability by technical feasibility, cost, content-specific limits, and the state of the art. For free-form text, one important implementation route is the implementation of a generative watermarking procedure, which poses a compliance problem that is hard to address. Strong watermarking is impossible against adaptive removal, while ordinary edits attenuate statistical evidence, and unmarked human text may overlap distributionally with machine output. This article develops an auditable alternative. First, it defines a description-length robustness profile. A finite-sample bound shows that detectable bias decays and that the required sample size grows with the inverse square of the decay rate. This replaces an unidentified Shannon-entropy constant with collision entropy. Second, it constructs label-conditional conformal prediction sets with separate false-attribution and false-exclusion levels, reporting ``watermark supported,'' ``not supported,'' or ``inconclusive''. Coverage is obtained as a finite-sample result and is class-conditional under exchangeability. A small reproducible simulation of a tournament watermark confirms both claims and shows that the surviving-token rule overstates the tolerable edit rate roughly twofold. The resulting premarket certificate, signed detector report, and postmarket recalibration protocol operationalize the Commission's 2026 Code of Practice without claiming universal robustness.

items.title: We Need to talk about AI: Software in Modern Heliophysics
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing how scientific software is developed, used and maintained. This presentation explores what that means for heliophysics, where published results depend on layers of software and the communities that sustain them. It considers opportunities for AI to support research alongside questions about scientific validation, human understanding, environmental costs, bias and equitable access. Examples from open-source development highlight how easier code generation can shift effort towards reviewers and maintainers. Solar Orbiter provides a setting for examining the appeal of independent development and the longer-term benefits of shared software. The presentation concludes with approaches to funding and organising shared infrastructure, and asks how the heliophysics community can preserve responsibility, learning and collaboration as AI becomes part of everyday scientific work.

items.title: What are the Ethical Considerations to Keep in Mind When Integrating New Educational Technologies into the Classroom?: A Case Study of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: New educational technologies—such as artificial intelligence (AI), generative AI, and wearable monitoring devices—are profoundly reshaping classroom ecologies. While they drive greater precision, personalization, and efficiency in teaching and learning, they also give rise to multiple ethical dilemmas, including data privacy breaches, the entrenchment of algorithmic bias, the alienation of teacher-student relationships, the erosion of student agency, and the blurring of responsibility attribution. Grounded in the fundamental educational mission of "fostering virtue and cultivating persons," this paper dialectically examines four core ethical tensions arising from the integration of new educational technologies into the classroom: efficiency versus humanism, empowerment versus rights, fairness versus bias, and autonomy versus discipline. It systematically distills five overarching ethical principles—rights protection, fairness and justice, humanistic authenticity, agency cultivation, and shared responsibility—and proposes a practical pathway characterized by technology for good, ethics-first design, and multi-stakeholder governance. Finally, this paper provides a critical evaluation of the structural friction and feasibility limits of these principles, aiming to establish a robust moral foundation for the beneficial integration of technology and education within the global landscape.

items.title: What Did the AI Take On? Characterizing Cognitive Delegation in LLM Reasoning
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often perform intermediate cognitive work while carrying out users' requests, yet it remains unclear which parts users intended to delegate and how they wanted to remain involved. This matters because consequential choices may go unnoticed, limiting users' ability to steer the process, while reviewing every step would make delegation burdensome. We examined this with 24 LLM users across three knowledge-work tasks, collecting 992 retrospective annotations of reasoning steps. From this, we developed taxonomies of LLM cognitive work, delegation enactment, and desired delegation protocols at the reasoning-step level. Our analysis revealed that participants viewed about half of all steps (48.6%) as AI-initiated, meaning the AI took on work they had not requested. Desired involvement varied with cognitive work and delegation enactment, even when contributions matched participants' intent. We propose design implications and sketches for supporting more deliberate cognitive delegation through flexible protocols and inspectable, revisable AI-initiated decisions.

items.title: What Do Borrower Workarounds Reveal? User-Derived Design Implications for Digital Finance in Indonesian Crowdlending
items.abstract: This study examines how Indonesian crowdlending borrowers navigate tensions among access, risk, and trust. It draws on interviews with 30 borrowersand uses an abductive, constructivist grounded-theory approach, with substantial intercoder reliability (Cohen’s kappa = 0.775). Four categories emerged: Paradoxical Necessity, Comparative Advantage Calculation, Risk-Exposure Management, and Institutional Legitimacy Navigation. Borrowers accommodate these tensions through temporal separation, cautious engagement, and legitimacy assessment. They preserve access by addressing immediate needs, comparing credit options, adjusting repayment practices after adverse experiences, and weighing regulatory status alongside platform terms and personal experience. Borrowers with longer or more adverse platform histories described more deliberate comparison, repayment management, and legitimacy assessment. However, the cross-sectional design cannot determine whether these differences reflect development over time or preexisting differences. Borrower workarounds indicate potential unmet design needs, especially in transparency, risk communication, and trust calibration, and provide borrower-derived implications for platform design and regulatory oversight.

items.title: When AI Education Moves Faster Than Teaching Practice: Teacher Labour Alienation in the Transitional Phase of AI Integration
items.abstract: Existing research on Artificial Intelligence in Education (AIED) has largely presupposed a mature landscape in which AI is fully embedded within schooling, whilst overlooking the initial transitional phase from conventional to AI-enabled instruction. Grounded in Marxist philosophy, this paper examines the central contradiction of this transitional period: namely, that social consciousness regarding the incorporation of AI into teaching has run considerably ahead of the material reality of instructional practice. From this disparity, three progressively intensified forms of alienation are derived: instructional performativity, wherein AI is reduced to a demonstration prop for open classes; the symbolic reification of AI, whereby it degenerates from a pedagogical aid into vacuous evaluative metrics; and reverse discipline over teachers by AI, such that quantifiable indicators come to serve as the primary measure of professional competence. Collectively, these three dimensions instantiate a Marxian cycle of alienation, characterised by a thoroughgoing estrangement from labour processes, labour products and species-being. The argument advanced here is that resolution of this crisis depends not upon further technological refinement, but rather upon restoring AI to its proper status as a productive force mediated by the historical agency of teachers themselves. Whilst the integration of AI into education presents a significant opportunity for pedagogical transformation, ultimate educational authority must remain vested in human practitioners. Focusing upon the alienation of teacher labour during this transitional moment, this study uncovers structural vulnerabilities latent within the AIED ecosystem via an analysis of these stratified alienated forms.

items.title: When AI Sounds Supportive: Comparing Conversational AI and Therapist Responses to Mental Health Disclosures
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Objectives To compare artificial intelligence (AI) and therapist responses to real‐world mental health (MH) disclosures and evaluate differences in empathy, safety practices and contextual usefulness. Methods We analysed 937 unique MH disclosures and 2749 therapist responses using the Counsel Chat dataset. For each disclosure, we generated a standardised AI response using a large language model. Responses were evaluated across empathy, safety and contextual usefulness measures using automated metrics, blinded human ratings of 120 therapist‐AI response pairs, mixed effects regression models, and qualitative analyses of disagreement cases. Results AI responses scored higher than therapist responses on automated empathy ( β = 0.30; p < 0.001), human‐rated empathy ( β = 0.38; p < 0.001), emotional validation ( β = 0.40; p < 0.001) and automated safety ( β = 0.25; p < 0.001). AI safety advantages were largest for self‐harm or suicide‐related disclosures. Therapists scored higher on specificity/personalisation ( β = −0.62; p < 0.001) and helpfulness ( β = −0.23; p = 0.013); overall quality did not differ significantly. Conclusions As conversational AI becomes an increasingly common source of MH support, AI responses may offer strengths in empathic communication and explicit safety‐oriented guidance, whereas therapist responses were rated more highly for personalisation and contextual usefulness. These findings highlight different strengths across AI and therapist responses while underscoring the need for caution in interpreting response quality as clinical effectiveness. They also point to a potential role for conversational AI as an accessible first point of support within broader MH care systems, particularly where timely professional support is limited.

items.title: When AI Stops Being a Tool and Becomes an Actor
items.abstract: When AI Stops Being a Tool and Becomes an Actor examines what changes when artificial intelligence moves beyond responding to human instructions and begins independently planning, using tools, accessing systems, and taking actions on a user's behalf. The report brings together research across six disciplines—artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, philosophy, law, economics, and computing infrastructure—to examine the emerging consequences of agentic AI. It investigates the technical difference between chatbots and agents; the security risks created by memory, tool access, and external communication; the philosophical problem of responsibility and agency; emerging legal questions around authorization and liability; the economic implications of agents negotiating and transacting on behalf of humans; and the infrastructure changes accompanying an increasingly machine-mediated internet. Rather than treating agentic AI as inherently good or bad, the report examines what current evidence actually establishes, where uncertainty remains, and where the conclusions of different fields begin to diverge. The report's central finding is that no single human, system, or institution is currently positioned to trace where a given agentic decision actually came from. Agentic decision-making is distributed across model behavior, deployment choices, authorization structures, legal frameworks, and infrastructure. This report is an independent research publication by Lodestar and is based on peer-reviewed research, preprints, government and legal materials, and industry reporting available as of September 2026. Where evidence relies on a simulation, a single source, or an unreviewed preprint, the report identifies that uncertainty directly.

Furthermore, the extensive deployment of service robots in reception services underscores the growing necessity for a comprehensive understanding of consumer reactions, particularly in scenarios where human assistance is either unavailable or replaced by automated systems. items.title: When Layer Selection Misleads Speech Depression Detection
items.abstract: Pretrained speech representations are increasingly used for depression detection, but selecting the best encoder layer on the same data used for evaluation biases reported performance. On DAIC-WOZ, with repeated nested cross-validation across five deep encoder families, naive best-of-25-layer probing inflates AUC by up to $0.09$. On shuffled labels over the \emph{real} latent representations, naive best-of-25 still reaches AUC $0.59$ versus $0.50$ under nested selection, and this bias grows with the number of probed layers and with smaller samples, isolating selection, not signal, as the cause. The effect replicates on a second clinical corpus and language (Androids, Italian). Under leakage-free selection, a fair comparison across representation families identifies a compact, task-aligned affect--prosody model as competitive with substantially more complex SSL, deep-learning, audio-LLM, and codec-based approaches, while using $\sim\!10^{3}\times$ fewer trainable downstream parameters. Extending the analysis to individual PHQ-8 symptoms shows that the same selection bias persists at this finer-grained level. We argue nested model-selection protocols should be standard when probing encoder layer representations on small clinical speech datasets.

items.title: When the AI Self Becomes the Ideal Self: A Systematic Review of AI-Enhanced Self-Discrepancy, Appearance Anxiety, and Protective Psychological Factors
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) appearance technologies, including beauty filters, augmented reality (AR) modification and generative avatars, have individualized digital self-presentation. Unlike traditional media, these technologies create self-referential appearance ideals that create novel forms of self-discrepancy and appearance anxiety. A systematic review was conducted in peer-reviewed databases for empirical studies published from 2021 to 2026 that studied self-representation, self-discrepancy, appearance distress, and protective psychological constructs within this context of AI, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Emergent patterns were identified by using the narrative thematic synthesis method across eligible studies. A total of eight empirical studies were found that fulfilled the inclusion criteria. The themes that emerged were as follows: (1) AI-enhanced self as a novel appearance ideal of the self; (2) self-discrepancy as an operative mechanism between the appearance of idealized and non-idealized selves and psychological distress; (3) contextually related and protective moderators; and (4) representation modality—between aestheticizing versus non-aestheticizing appearance modalities and psychological distress. The findings from the synthesis showed that self-discrepancy, social self-comparison, and self-objectification are the three main routes for appearance anxiety. Theoretically, these non-idealizing avatars, high self-similarity, and goal-oriented use contexts were considered as protective buffers but were not consistently quantified. Most importantly, there was no empirical study that directly assessed positive body image constructs or body appreciation. The current research mainly focuses on the pathology aspect of AI appearance technology, and positive body image is not investigated. Empirical studies should be conducted in the future with the clear aim of examining if constructive, nonidealized relationships with the technologically enhanced body can foster psychological resilience, and if so, how.

items.title: Widening or Deepening? How Firms Integrate AI and Large Language Models into Research and Discovery
items.abstract: Multiple firms spanning expertise from material science and computational chemistry to pharmaceuticals have started investing into Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to streamline and expedite their Research and Discovery (R&D) process; however, the effects of this newfound integration of AI into R&D remain unclear as it is yet to be understood whether it is changing how the process is conducted versus simply accelerating the process. This study utilizes qualitative data collected from seven semi-structured interviews with interviewees with expertise spanning from corporate research and startups to innovation economics in order to analyze the central question: does the integration of AI in R&D deepen research in already explored areas by accelerating it or does it widen the directions of research and introduce novel directions? Across all interviews, the most common limitation noted in AI’s integration in R&D was human validation. Regarding the central question, the results skewed towards the deepening trend. Many interviewees mentioned that the current usage of AI causes its integration to only accelerate and improve the discovery within research directions already explored; however, interviewees explained that this was a trend based on the methodology of R&D used by most firms rather than a technological barrier of the tool itself. These results suggest that firms and policymakers should thoroughly evaluate the productivity increase of AI rather than its potential and focus on solving the several bottlenecks still not tackled by AI: validation, human judgement, and physical experimentation.

items.title: Wings or shackles? Artificial intelligence and Chinese corporate internationalization
items.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence’s (AI) influence on corporate operations is receiving increasing social attention. Does AI significantly influence the international expansion of enterprises? Design/methodology/approach Based on theories such as multinational corporations, this study selects relevant data from Chinese-listed companies spanning the years 2011–2019, with a particular emphasis on how artificial intelligence directly influences the scope and degree of corporate internationalization. This study also considers the moderating effects of CEO information technology background (ITCEO), ESG performance and external regional environmental regulations. Findings The research results indicate that artificial intelligence improves the scope and degree of internationalization performance of enterprises. Heterogeneity analysis found that artificial intelligence has different impacts on state-owned enterprises and private enterprises. The CEO’s expertise in IT serves as a positive moderating factor, enhancing the direct correlation between artificial intelligence and the scope, as well as the degree of their company’s internationalization efforts. ESG performance serves as a positive moderating factor, enhancing the direct correlation between artificial intelligence and the scope of their company’s internationalization efforts. The external regional environmental regulations serve as a negative moderating factor. Originality/value This study innovatively integrates artificial intelligence (AI) into the analysis of both the scope and degree of enterprise internationalization, thereby enriching the literature on AI and its applications in business strategies. By incorporating AI, this research broadens the theoretical and empirical insights into the determinants affecting the scope and degree of corporate internationalization. This study systematically examines the moderating effects of CEOs with IT backgrounds, corporate ESG performance and regional environmental regulations, thereby extending the scope of research on the determinants of internationalization.

items.title: Workforce Strategies in the Age of AI: Designing Job Roles for A Post-Automation Economy
items.abstract: With the advancement in technology, the present process of business operations and functions are not stable or predictable anymore and this allows the labour force to exist in a complex and uncertain market. Consequently, the need for employees to develop their own capacity to innovate, adapt to change, and manage this emerging instability is germane. There are several market dynamics that impact labour market, such as demographic development, the competitiveness of the nations’ economy, globalization and last but not the least is technological change or digitalization. Research showed that the technological revolution, however, is of great significance. The technological transformation is a prevailing factor out of the four listed (Messina. Artificial Intelligence and digital transformation have revolutionized the strategies that are deployed by both public and private organizations to relate with their customers, and specifically how companies run their business, how they conceive their business approach and how they consolidate their operations. It is about integrating digital technologies, such as social, mobile, analytics and cloud, in the service of transforming how businesses work. Although it is important to state that the incorporation of digital technology into business processes has become very imperative for the survival and competitive advantage of contemporary organizations, Human Capital Management (HCM) focuses on the performance of the organization emphasizing its role as a solution to business problems in the post-automation economy. Therefore, designing job roles in the post-automation economy is a strategic asset to businesses contributing to the competitive advantage of organizations. Thus, the entirety of this paper is centered on a more varied, more people-oriented with the responsibility of designing diverse, challenging jobs in the post-automation economy to keep the human element more active and engaged in their work without redundancy. The paper strongly maintained that Human Capital Management is to assume more active roles in handling the post-automation, digitalization and the age of AI era in ensuring that the human element is skilled and knowledgeable to meet the future needs of the organizations

items.title: Xaurora: Generative Weather Forecasting with Denoising Stochastic Interpolants from a Foundation Model Prior
items.abstract: Deep learning has revolutionised weather forecasting in recent years, especially through atmospheric foundation models, which offer competitive skill for a fraction of the computational costs of classic physics-based models. However, most existing foundation models are deterministic, limiting the generation of large ensembles for accurate uncertainty quantification, extreme weather risk assessment, and long-range weather forecasting. Furthermore, these models incur a large, often prohibitive, computational overhead to train from scratch. To address these shortcomings, we turn a pretrained deterministic prior model, namely the Aurora foundation model, into a generative ensemble-prediction model. To that end, we introduce a novel generative method, Denoising Stochastic Interpolants, combined with a replay buffer for Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) rollout, enabling probabilistic training of SDE trajectories. Our stochastic foundation model, Xaurora, is finetuned from the small Aurora version, yet it approaches the state-of-the-art on global ensemble metrics and is competitive with the large version of Aurora. Our method is parameter and sample efficient, and generates skilful 15-day forecasts in 13 minutes. Our results demonstrate that deterministic foundation models can be efficiently extended into even stronger stochastic models.

items.title: Zero-shot mineral segmentation in reflected-light microscopy using the segment anything model
items.abstract: Automated mineral segmentation underpins quantitative mineralogy and stereological characterization, but supervised deep-learning methods require annotated data and may generalize poorly across mineralogical domains. This study evaluated the Segment Anything Model (SAM), a general-purpose foundation model, for reflected-light microscopy (RLM) mineral-image analysis in a purely zero-shot setting, without task-specific training, fine-tuning, or domain adaptation. Two complementary case studies were conducted. First, three SAM encoder variants (ViT-B, ViT-L, and ViT-H) were evaluated on publicly available iron-ore (FeM) and copper-ore (Cu) RLM datasets using SEM-derived reference masks. SAM achieved mean F1-scores of 0.77–0.88, with ViT-L and ViT-H reaching 93–94% of the previously reported supervised DeepLabv3+ F1-score benchmark for FeM and approximately 93% for Cu. Second, SAM was applied to polarized RLM image stacks of dolomite to assess its influence on downstream stereological characterization. No significant differences from the gradient-based method were detected for any RGB configuration or PCA ViT-B in major or minor intercept length or bireflectance. The largest deviations occurred for PCA-preprocessed ViT-H, with median major and minor intercept lengths approximately 21% and 17% higher, respectively, and bireflectance approximately 16% lower. No significant method-dependent difference was detected in principal anisotropy orientation. These results show that zero-shot SAM can support mineral-image segmentation and downstream stereological characterization without annotated training data, while highlighting the influence of preprocessing and encoder choice on the derived grain representation

items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into social practice has been accompanied by the emergence of new forms of unlawful conduct, requiring a reconsideration of traditional institutions of criminal law. The most challenging cases for criminal-law qualification arise where an AI system operates with partial or full autonomy, independently determining the means of achieving a goal set by a human. In such situations, establishing a causal link between the user’s conduct and the resulting socially dangerous consequences does not, in itself, constitute a sufficient basis for criminal liability, thereby raising the issue of the limits of subjective attribution. Based on the normative framework of the 2021 Criminal Code of the Republic of Armenia governing guilt, mistake as to factual circumstances, harm caused without guilt, and justified risk, the article argues that AI cannot be recognized as an independent subject of criminal liability. To determine the limits of criminal-law attribution, the author distinguishes three models of criminally relevant use of AI: the instrumental model (AI as a means of implementing criminal intent), the risk-based model (the use of AI in circumstances where the possibility of a socially dangerous consequence is foreseen or ought to be foreseen), and the autonomous-result model (the occurrence of a result that was not encompassed by the person’s intent and whose possibility the person was neither required nor able to foresee). The principle of controlled autonomy formulated in the article makes it possible to determine the boundary between culpable harm caused by a human and a result of the autonomous operation of an intelligent system that cannot be attributed to that person.

items.abstract: This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations for using marketing analytics as a tool for strategic decision-making in advertising management in the context of sustainable development. The relevance of this study stems from the digital transformation of marketing activities, the growth in data volumes, the increasing complexity of consumer behavior models, and the need to shift from evaluating advertising activities primarily based on economic criteria to a comprehensive consideration of the economic, social, and environmental outcomes of advertising strategies. The role of marketing analytics as a component of the information and analytical support for strategic advertising management is substantiated; its functional purpose lies in transforming marketing data into relevant information for justifying, selecting, and adjusting strategic decisions. The functional purpose of descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive analytics in the process of developing advertising strategies is revealed. The paper identifies opportunities for applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, and predictive modeling technologies to segment target audiences, personalize advertising messages, forecast consumer behavior, and optimize advertising investments. The paper justifies the need to integrate the principles of sustainable development into the system for evaluating the effectiveness of advertising strategies. It proposes a system of indicators structured around economic, social, and environmental components, which makes it possible to take into account – alongside the commercial effectiveness of advertising investments – brand trust, responsibility and transparency of advertising communications, the impact on the formation of sustainable consumption patterns, the environmental impact of advertising activities, and the risks of greenwashing. For a comprehensive assessment, an integral index of sustainable advertising strategy performance (ISRAS) is proposed, which involves aggregating normalized indicators of economic, social, and environmental performance and can be used for a multi-criteria comparison of alternative advertising strategies. To illustrate the ISRAS application algorithm, a demonstration calculation was performed using two hypothetical scenarios of IKEA’s advertising strategy and model normalized values. Scientific and practical recommendations have been formulated for improving the strategic decision-making process in advertising management based on an integrated analytical and strategic approach that encompasses analytical diagnosis, the formulation of strategic alternatives, their multi-criteria evaluation, the selection and implementation of an advertising strategy, monitoring, and strategic adjustments. The feasibility of transitioning from a piecemeal assessment of advertising campaign effectiveness to a comprehensive evaluation of the sustained effectiveness of advertising strategies has been substantiated. The potential for integrating marketing analytics and the principles of sustainable development has been identified to enhance the soundness of strategic advertising decisions, optimize marketing resources, strengthen consumer trust, minimize reputational and environmental risks, and create long-term value for the enterprise, consumers, and society.

items.abstract: 本文构建一套以爱因斯坦科学方法论为根基,融合六大原创核心原则,适配人-AI协同模式的理论物理研究范式。 该范式以刚性惯性原理为核心约束,通过工程化的流程设计,实现从现象关联到公理确立、从模型构建到理论拓展的全链路严谨推导,具备公理固化、过程可复现、逻辑可追溯、错误可排查的显著特征。 This study constructs a theoretical physics research paradigm rooted in Einstein's scientific methodology, integrating six original core principles, and adapted to human-AI collaborative mode. With the Rigidity-Inertia Principle as the core constraint, this paradigm achieves rigorous derivation across the full chain from phenomenon correlation to axiom establishment, from model construction to theoretical expansion through engineered process design. It features axiom solidification, reproducible processes, traceable logic, and debuggable errors.

items.title: “Word‐By‐Word” or “Line‐By‐Line” Presentation? How Response Generation Dynamics in Generative AI Influence User Acceptance
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Generative AI systems are increasingly integrated into various user support and decision‐making contexts. While extensive research has explored user acceptance of generative AI across domains, less is known about how its inherent presentation features influence such acceptance. This study investigates how the presentation format of generative AI responses—high‐dynamism formats (word‐by‐word) versus low‐dynamism formats (line‐by‐line)—affects users' willingness to accept its output. Three experiments, across various contexts, including daily question‐answering, online shopping, and crowdfunding platforms, tested how the dynamic presentation of generative AI responses influences users' willingness to accept its output. The results demonstrate that users exhibit greater receptivity when generative AI responses are presented in high‐dynamism formats. This effect occurs because dynamic presentation enhances users' feelings of immersion. Furthermore, we find that users' situational need for understanding moderates this immersion‐based mechanism. Specifically, the positive indirect effect of dynamic presentation on willingness to accept the output through feelings of immersion is attenuated in high need‐for‐understanding contexts, where users tend to prioritize content quality, accuracy, and diagnosticity. In contrast, this indirect effect is amplified in low need‐for‐understanding contexts, where users are more receptive to the experiential and interactional qualities of dynamic presentation. This research contributes to the literature on the effectiveness of dynamic presentation and provides novel insights into the factors influencing user acceptance of generative AI outputs. Our findings highlight the importance of tailoring output presentation methods based on individual user characteristics and task‐specific cognitive demands.

items.title: 346 Dead - and Boeing Is Still Asking Pilots to Work Around the Software
items.abstract: The Boeing 737 MAX disasters killed 346 people and exposed profound failures involving aircraft design, automation, human-factors assumptions, corporate safety culture, and federal regulatory oversight. This article examines those failures against the emergence of a new flight-management-system software defect capable of disengaging vertical navigation (VNAV) during certain missed-approach sequences on affected 737 MAX aircraft. Rather than equating the VNAV issue with the catastrophic MCAS failures, the analysis considers a more fundamental question: whether Boeing and the Federal Aviation Administration have adequately incorporated the lessons of the MAX accidents when known automation deficiencies can still be mitigated through increased pilot workload while permanent engineering corrections remain pending. The investigation further examines Boeing’s criminal-accountability history, including the federal fraud charge, deferred prosecution agreement, subsequent determination that Boeing breached that agreement, proposed guilty plea, and eventual non-prosecution agreement. Particular attention is given to Boeing’s extensive political presence, campaign and inaugural contributions, federal lobbying, regulatory relationships, and its selection for major next-generation U.S. fighter programs. No evidence examined establishes a quid pro quo between Boeing’s political activities, prosecutorial outcomes, or defense contracts; however, the record reveals substantial structural interdependence between Boeing and the federal institutions responsible for regulating, prosecuting, and purchasing from the company. The article argues that after 346 deaths, reliance upon pilots to compensate procedurally for correctable automation deficiencies deserves exceptional scrutiny and that Boeing’s strategic importance should not insulate the corporation or its decision-makers from meaningful regulatory and criminal accountability.

items.title: A Bibliometrics of the Analysis Methods of 3D Printed Concrete Structures
items.abstract: 3D concrete printing (3DCP) has revolutionized the construction industry, allowing for the produc-tion of complex geometries with greater efficiency and sustainability. This is despite ongoing challenges with structural reliability and long-term performance, which are due to the material's anisotropic properties and layer interfaces.This study performed a bibliometric analysis of the literature on the structural analysis of 3DCP, using VOSviewer to identify research trends and gaps. The methodology included a keyword search in the Scopus database, which resulted in 108 selected articles after a rigorous screening process. The results in-dicate a significant increase in 3DCP research since 2018, with a projected peak of 40 articles published in 2025. A co-occurrence analysis of keywords revealed a concentration on "concretes," "concrete printings," and "finite element method," highlighting research into material failure and behavior. The 108 works, au-thored by 374 individuals, were distributed across 8 clusters, with 23 papers showing co-authorship. Maximil-iano Cremonesi, Liberato Ferrara, and Giacomo Rizzieri had the strongest collaborations between 2024 and 2025. China and the United States lead in publications, with 37 and 12 articles, respectively, and China also leads in collaborations with 14. The Journal of Building Engineering was the most relevant journal, with 11 publications. Despite these advancements, the study points to significant gaps, such as the need for more so-phisticated numerical models to simulate interlayer and multi-scale interactions. The integration of structural reinforcements and a better understanding of the long-term durability of 3DCP are also critical challenges. Furthermore, there is a major opportunity for research in multifunctional materials and the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning to optimize design and predict performance, thereby boosting sus-tainability in 3DCP.

items.title: A Critical African Examination of Nick Bostrom's Conception of the Problem of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has generated profound philosophical questions concerning intelligence, agency, autonomy, responsibility, human values, technological power, and the future of humanity. Among contemporary philosophers, Nick Bostrom has provided one of the most systematic philosophical analyses of the long-term risks associated with advanced artificial intelligence. His conception of the problem is principally concerned with the possibility that artificial general intelligence may develop into superintelligence whose cognitive and strategic capacities surpass those of human beings. The central difficulty, according to Bostrom, is not merely whether machines can think, but whether humanity can retain meaningful control over machines that may eventually become more intelligent and strategically capable than their creators. This article critically examined Bostrom's conception of the problem of artificial intelligence, focusing on his notions of superintelligence, existential risk, the orthogonality thesis, instrumental convergence, and the control problem. It argued that Bostrom's analysis provides an important conceptual foundation for contemporary debates on artificial intelligence safety and alignment but requires philosophical supplementation when considered from an African perspective. In particular, the individualistic assumptions that can underlie some formulations of artificial intelligence ethics require enrichment through African conceptions of communal responsibility, relational personhood, human dignity, and social embeddedness. The article concluded that Bostrom's conception of artificial intelligence is philosophically valuable as a theory of technological control and existential risk, but its relevance to Africa is strengthened when integrated with relational and communitarian conceptions of personhood and responsibility. Keywords: Artificial intelligence, Nick Bostrom, superintelligence, existential risk, alignment, control problem, African philosophy.

items.title: A Framework for Automated Multi-Source Satellite Data Analytics and LLM-Based Report Generation
items.abstract: This paper presents the workflow for building an automated ArcGIS Pro tool using ArcPy to extract the Land Surface Temperature (LST) from Landsat 7, 8 and 9 datasets. The tool eliminates the need for manual band selection and repetitive raster computations by automating the multi-step workflow of radiometric calibration, NDVI-based emissivity correction, and thermal conversion. In addition to supporting batch and single-scene processing, the tool has an optional Large Language Model (LLM) for statistical result interpretation and reporting. Depending on batch size, the tool reduced the processing time from around 11-58 minutes when done manually to around 4-11 minutes using the tool. We tested the tool with data from Ras Al Khaimah (RAK) in the UAE, and the LST obtained for Ras Al Khaimah ranged from approximately 25C to 50C, demonstrating an accurate LST mapping compatible with the weather conditions of RAK. In summary, our tool reduces human errors and improves processing accuracy and efficiency for thermal and environmental remote sensing applications, in addition to providing an interactive LLM-based interface for result interpretation.

items.title: A generative AI decision-making tool for interactive greenspace design using a pollinator habitat indicator
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in landscape architecture to accelerate design development and enhance stakeholder engagement. This study presents a new landscape concept design tool to support collaborative greenspace problem-solving by integrating rapid scenario generation with a Pollinator Habitat Indicator (PHI). We define this as the PHI-AI Landscape Design Tool. The model combines text-to-image generative workflows with a simplified pollinator-oriented reference that compares AI-generated scenarios based on broad landscape cover composition. The PHI-AI Landscape Design Tool generated varied concept layouts with planting and pathway configurations responsive to descriptive prompts and user-defined parameters. It generates layout variations that reflect visually coherent planting configurations, and circulation connections to existing infrastructure for user functionality. This enables the rapid production of multiple design alternatives that remain legible, adaptable, and flexible to human-controlled editing prompts for stakeholder engagement. This study offers a framework for integrating a simplified ecological reference into the planning phase of landscape design.
